title: Escape to Bhutan | From Sacred Trails to Highland Tales
highlights: Visit Chimi Lhakhang, known as the "Temple of Fertility," revered for its cultural significance and blessings for fertility and childbirth.
Witness Drukgyel Dzong in Bhutan, a historic fortress built in 1649 to celebrate victory over Tibetan invaders.
Experience the charm of Bhutan as you visit ancient monasteries, indulge in vibrant culture and admire the Himalayan landscapes across beautiful destinations like Thimphu, Punakha, and Paro.
Hike to Tiger's Nest in Paro, a sacred monastery nestled on a cliffside, known for its religious significance and stunning Himalayan views.
Explore Motithang Takin Preserve, and observe Bhutan’s national animal, Takin in its natural habitat.
overview: Tucked in the lap of the Eastern Himalayas, Bhutan is adorned with scenic landscapes, enchanting ambience and enthralling peaks. Believe it or not, but this quaint country is a cult for the adventure junkies and nature lovers. With plenitude of options for the adrenaline junkies, it also offers nature tours.

know_before_you_go: Cancellation After Rescheduling: Clients who reschedule their tours or treks but later decide to cancel will be subject to our standard cancellation policy. Any rescheduling fees paid will be non-refundable.
Images are for representation purpose only.

ID Proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

days.title: Arrival in Paro | Transfer to Thimphu | Leisure Day
days.desc: Welcome to Bhutan! Upon your arrival at Paro International Airport, get driven to your hotel in Thimpu. Check in and spend your day at leisure. You can visit the Royal Botanical Garden, showcasing a diverse range of native flora amidst serene surroundings. You can also explore Ludrong Memorial Garden, established to honour the memory of Ludrong Dorji, a revered figure known for his contributions to Bhutanese culture. Later, return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, enjoy a sightseeing tour of Thimphu. Begin with a visit to the National Memorial Chorten, a tribute to Bhutan’s 3rd king, Jigme Dorji Wangchuck. Next, marvel at the 177-ft tall Buddha Dordenma Statue at Kuenselphodrang. Explore the Motithang Takin Preserve to see Bhutan's unique national animal, and then visit the impressive Tashichho Dzong. Get insight into the rich cultural heritage at Simtokha Dzong and the Handicrafts Market. Later, get transferred to your hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Punakha via Dochula Pass | Stay & Sightseeing
days.desc: After checking out of your hotel, get transferred to Punakha. En route, make a stop at Dochula Pass, and admire panoramic views of the majestic Himalayas. Upon arrival in Punakha, visit Chimi Lhakhang, a famous temple, also known as "temple of fertility". Next, explore Punakha Dzong, an architectural marvel situated at the confluence of two rivers, Pho Chu and Mo Chu. Finally, get driven to your hotel in Punakha, check in and enjoy your overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Paro | Stay & Sightseeing
days.desc: In the morning, check out of your hotel get driven to Paro. Upon arrival, check in at your hotel and get ready for a sightseeing tour of Paro. Explore Drukgyel Dzong, a historic fortress built to celebrate Bhutan's triumph over Tibetan invaders. Next, visit the ancient Buddhist temple, Kyichu Lhakhang, one of Bhutan's oldest temples with profound cultural significance. After the tour, board your transfer back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Day Trip to Tiger’s Nest
days.desc: Today, explore Ta Dzong, the National Museum, which houses a remarkable collection of Bhutanese art, textiles, weapons, and religious artifacts. Then, prepare yourself for an adventurous trek to Taktsang Monastery, famously known as Tiger's Nest. Get driven to Satsam Chencho Tshongkhang and enjoy a trek through pine forests and past prayer flags. Alternatively, you can choose to take a horse ride to the monastery (extra cost). Afterward, get transferred to your hotel for an overnight stay.
